expected.rationale: The approach — 175-200 yards across an ocean chasm from a bluff to a small, canted green — is repeatedly framed as a precision/club-selection puzzle rather than a power test. Jack Nicklaus called it 'the finest second shot in golf' for its demand of an exact line and number into a small target, not for its length.
sources: Golf.com, 'How Pebble Beach altered — and safeguarded! — dramatic 8th hole'
Golf.com, 'What you can learn from the par-4 8th hole at Pebble Beach'
Golf Digest, 'The 7 most spectacular but daunting shots at Pebble Beach'
